items.title: Image: expose requested versus actual dimensions and explicit size mismatch diagnostics
items.body:
## Context
Observed while using tny to create and iterate on five Omarchy ultrawide wallpapers. The workflow used parallel `tny ask` ideation, `tny image generate` / `tny image edit`, visual inspection, and ImageMagick exports. Installed CLI reports `tny 0.9.0`; exact root causes have not been diagnosed.

## Problem
Requests targeting 3440 × 1440 returned generated images around 1935–1940 × 811–812. We had to inspect files and upscale them to the desktop resolution. This does not establish whether the cause is a provider limit, parameter translation, or provider behavior.

## Proposed scope
Define a dimensions contract shared by CLI and image tools. Distinguish requested size, effective provider request, actual generated size, and any final export size. Surface unsupported sizes or substitutions explicitly; do not describe resized output as native generation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Structured results include requested and actual dimensions, effective provider size when available, MIME type, and any resize/crop operation.
- [ ] A mismatch yields an actionable warning in human output and a machine-readable status in JSON.
- [ ] Document provider-specific size support and behavior for unsupported requests; an optional strict mode fails rather than silently accepting a mismatch.
- [ ] Tests cover exact matches, mismatches, auto size, unsupported requests, and separation of native versus exported dimensions.

items.title: Subagents: diagnose creation failures and provide actionable launcher errors
items.body:
## Context
Observed while using tny to create and iterate on five Omarchy ultrawide wallpapers. The workflow used parallel `tny ask` ideation, `tny image generate` / `tny image edit`, visual inspection, and ImageMagick exports. Installed CLI reports `tny 0.9.0`; exact root causes have not been diagnosed.

## Observed behavior
Session-backed `subagent` creation failed during parallel wallpaper ideation. Both named child IDs and an unnamed creation attempt were tried. Parallel `tny ask` subprocesses worked as a workaround.

The exact error payload and a minimal reproducer are not included in this report. Treat this as a triage report, not a confirmed diagnosis of the launcher internals.

## Investigation / expected behavior
- [ ] Reproduce child creation from an active agent session under the all-tools profile; test named and automatically assigned IDs against the documented schema.
- [ ] Determine whether failure comes from invocation validation, session creation, environment inheritance, provider startup, or unsupported execution mode.
- [ ] Supported creation returns a durable child ID and working inspect/message/lifecycle operations.
- [ ] Invalid or unsupported calls return a stable error code and actionable explanation, including the valid invocation or supported fallback.
- [ ] Add regression tests for the identified failure and negative-path diagnostics; ensure errors do not expose credentials.

## Impact
The parent had to replace child-agent orchestration with shell processes and custom monitoring. This failure was separate from image-provider generation.

items.title: Jobs: durable background execution and bounded batches for ask and image commands
items.body:
## Context
Observed while using tny to create and iterate on five Omarchy ultrawide wallpapers. The workflow used parallel `tny ask` ideation, `tny image generate` / `tny image edit`, visual inspection, and ImageMagick exports. Installed CLI reports `tny 0.9.0`; exact root causes have not been diagnosed.

## Problem
Parallel ideation and image rendering required custom subprocess launches, log files, and repeated `sleep` / `cat` polling. It was difficult to obtain one structured view of completion, failures, and output artifacts.

## Proposed scope
Provide first-class durable jobs usable by shell scripts and agent tools. Command names are illustrative: submit/background, status, wait, cancel, and batch. Support `tny ask` and image generate/edit without conflating their lifecycles.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Submission returns a job ID and persisted metadata/log locations immediately.
- [ ] Status and wait expose queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled states, exit/error information, and artifact paths in structured output.
- [ ] Jobs remain inspectable after the submitting CLI exits; interrupted jobs receive an explicit state rather than appearing to run forever.
- [ ] Cancellation cleans up owned child processes without affecting unrelated work.
- [ ] Batch execution supports bounded concurrency, per-item results, and retrying selected failures without regenerating successes.
- [ ] Tests cover mixed outcomes, cancellation, interrupted submitters, concurrency limits, and output-path collisions.

## Related
Coordinate event output with #66 rather than introducing an incompatible JSONL schema. This is useful independently of fixing session-backed subagent creation.

items.title: Image: optional exact-canvas exports and contact sheets while preserving originals
items.body:
## Context
Observed while using tny to create and iterate on five Omarchy ultrawide wallpapers. The workflow used parallel `tny ask` ideation, `tny image generate` / `tny image edit`, visual inspection, and ImageMagick exports. Installed CLI reports `tny 0.9.0`; exact root causes have not been diagnosed.

## Problem
Generation alone did not finish the wallpaper task. External ImageMagick commands were required to make exact 3440 × 1440 exports, larger copies, and a multi-image contact sheet.

## Proposed scope
An optional, explicit post-processing/export layer, separate from provider generation. Offer target dimensions and fit/crop/pad policy plus contact-sheet creation. An external-tool integration is acceptable if dependencies and failures are clear; do not silently add post-processing to existing generation behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Exact output dimensions can be requested with an explicit aspect-ratio policy and crop alignment.
- [ ] Native generated originals are retained separately; overwrite behavior is explicit and safe.
- [ ] Metadata records source dimensions, target dimensions, scaling/cropping, and source artifact linkage.
- [ ] Exported/upscaled files are never presented as native-resolution generations.
- [ ] Contact sheets support multiple artifacts with optional labels and deterministic ordering.
- [ ] Tests verify dimensions, aspect-ratio handling, preservation of originals, missing dependencies, and partial export failures.

items.title: Image: connect generation results to capability-aware visual previews
items.body:
## Context
Observed while using tny to create and iterate on five Omarchy ultrawide wallpapers. The workflow used parallel `tny ask` ideation, `tny image generate` / `tny image edit`, visual inspection, and ImageMagick exports. Installed CLI reports `tny 0.9.0`; exact root causes have not been diagnosed.

## Problem
Image generation returned file metadata, but visual QA required separate `read_image` calls for every artifact. Checking composition and the generated OMARCHY lettering was essential; successful file creation alone did not prove quality.

## Proposed scope
Build on #98 (typed image-attachment control channel) and #50 (provider image capability gating). This issue covers the generation-to-review experience, not another attachment transport implementation. Provide an optional preview/attach behavior, or a directly consumable image artifact reference, in both CLI and tool workflows where supported.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A successful generation can explicitly attach a preview for the agent's next visual review, using the shared attachment mechanism.
- [ ] Metadata-only behavior remains available for scripts and non-vision backends.
- [ ] Results identify the full-resolution artifact and any downsampled preview separately.
- [ ] Unsupported vision/transport modes give clear fallback instructions without losing a successfully generated artifact.
- [ ] Preview failures are distinguishable from generation failures; neither is silently interpreted as visual approval.
- [ ] Tests cover attachment timing, capability gating, bounded payloads, and CLI/tool parity.

items.title: Image: persist generation manifests and reference lineage for repeatable iteration
items.body:
## Context
Observed while using tny to create and iterate on five Omarchy ultrawide wallpapers. The workflow used parallel `tny ask` ideation, `tny image generate` / `tny image edit`, visual inspection, and ImageMagick exports. Installed CLI reports `tny 0.9.0`; exact root causes have not been diagnosed.

## Problem
Prompts, reference mappings, logs, generated originals, and exports had to be organized manually in a Python workflow and JSON files. Iterating on a favorite image depended on reconstructing those associations.

## Proposed scope
Persist a versioned manifest per generate/edit operation. Permit subsequent edits to reference an earlier artifact/job, while keeping explicit file paths supported. Reproducibility here means recording inputs and lineage, not promising bit-identical provider output.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Record prompt, reference paths and content hashes, provider/model, quality, requested/effective/actual dimensions, timestamps, result status, and artifact paths.
- [ ] Record seed or provider request ID only when actually supplied by the provider; do not fabricate unavailable metadata.
- [ ] Edits and exports link to their source artifacts; manifests distinguish native outputs from derived copies.
- [ ] Manifest writes are atomic, schema-versioned, and safe under parallel runs; failed operations retain useful diagnostic state.
- [ ] A documented rerun/edit flow can consume recorded settings, with explicit overrides and clear warnings for missing references.
- [ ] Do not persist credentials; document prompt/reference privacy and provide control over manifest persistence.
- [ ] Tests cover round trips, lineage, moved/missing inputs, concurrent writes, and failed generation.

related_non_scope_issues.title: CLI: add canonical JSONL event stream mode for scripts
related_non_scope_issues.body:
## Goal

Make `tny` a first-class Unix/scriptable agent harness without requiring stderr scraping or waiting for one final JSON object.

## Scope

Add an event-streaming mode such as `tny ask --events=jsonl` backed by the canonical public event schema. Add a progress control such as `--progress=none` so successful machine-mode runs can keep stderr empty.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] stdout emits exactly one canonical event object per line in order.
- [ ] After a successful turn start, exactly one `turn_end` event is emitted.
- [ ] Machine events contain stable error/usage/tool/permission fields and no human decoration.
- [ ] `--progress=none` suppresses normal human tool/status stderr output.
- [ ] Existing Markdown and final `--json` modes remain compatible.
- [ ] Startup/config failures have a documented machine-readable option/shape.

## Verification

- [ ] Strict mock transcript matches libtny event ordering.
- [ ] Pipe/slow-consumer tests.
- [ ] Cancellation, permission, error, tool and usage fixtures.
- [ ] Shell examples in docs.

related_non_scope_issues.title: Runner: typed control channel with client roles for `tny ask-user` and `tny image attach`
related_non_scope_issues.body:
Part of the shell-first native loop plan (see epic).

## Goal
A typed control channel on the session socket (`<session>/sock`, ADR 0053) so a subprocess started by the `terminal` tool can ask the human a free-text question or attach an image to the next request. This is what makes `tny ask-user` and `tny image attach` cross-platform: the transport is tny's own socket, not AppleScript or `/dev/tty`.

## Problems found in review
- **Deadlock.** `terminal` blocks synchronously in its own poll loop (`src/core/tools_shell.c:101-124`) while the runner only accepts socket clients in its outer loop (`src/core/runner.c` `rn_accept`). A child that connects and waits for an answer never gets serviced.
- **No client roles.** Every connected client can currently send turn, cancel, permission, and end operations (`src/core/runner.c` ~708). A tool-role client must be limited to its own ops.
- **Image timing.** A request processed only after `terminal` returns can miss the immediately following provider POST; it must be queued through the existing pending-image path (`src/core/tools.c` ~510, ADR 0008) before the batch completes.
- **Not universal.** `tny acp` server mode, `--ephemeral`, wasm, and the macOS in-process fallback have no runner socket (ADR 0053 §9). Those modes need a frontend-callback adapter or a clean unsupported error; the socket is not the portable contract.

## Scope
- `src/core/runner.c`, `src/core/session.c`, `src/core/tools_shell.c`, `src/core/tools_ext.c`, ADR 0053 amendment.
- `terminal` exports the **resolved** socket path as `TNY_SESSION_SOCK` (deep paths have a fallback, `src/core/runner.c:258`) plus the session id into the child env.
- Handshake with roles `owner | observer | tool`; per-role op allowlist; correlation ids.
- Ops: `{"op":"ask_user","id":..,"question":..}` answered only by the owning frontend (observers cannot answer); `{"op":"image_attach","id":..,"path":..}` validated (path inside allowed roots, magic bytes) and ACKed.
- The terminal wait loop pumps only control ops and owner replies while a child runs; it never re-enters backend dispatch. Precedent: ACP's bounded nested pump (`src/backends/acp/acp_turn.c` ~192).
- New CLI verbs `tny ask-user QUESTION` and `tny image attach PATH`: with no socket they print one line to stderr and exit 1, never grab the TTY.

## Acceptance criteria
- `tests/test_runner.c` gains bidirectional split-boundary framing, role enforcement, correlation, disconnect-fails-closed, and a no-deadlock test with a child blocked on `ask_user` during `terminal`.
- `ask_user` returns arbitrary text, replacing today's yes/no via the permission hook (`src/core/tools_ext.c:332-342`).
- `tny acp` maps `ask_user` to the ACP question callback, not the socket.

## Dependencies
None to start; the in-process intercept issue depends on this for the non-intercepted (nested script) path.

related_non_scope_issues.title: Native loop: gate read_image and --image on a provider image capability
related_non_scope_issues.body:
## Problem

Native-loop images are a first-class tool (`read_image`, alias `vision`) that injects user-role `image_url` parts ([ADR 0008](https://github.com/thehumanworks/tny/blob/main/docs/adr/0008-native-loop-images.md)). That only works when the **provider** can accept those parts.

Today the schema always advertises `read_image`:

- `SCHEMA_JSON` in `src/core/tools.c` includes `read_image` for every native-loop provider.
- `read_file` always tells the model to use `read_image` on png/jpeg/gif/webp (`src/core/tools_fs.c`, `src/core/tools_ssh.c`).
- `tools_flush_images` then posts a user message with `image_url` data URLs (`src/core/image.c`).

Many OpenAI-compatible endpoints reject `image_url` / `input_image` (text-only grok proxy, small ollama/llama.cpp models, some routers). The model still calls `read_image`, the pixels are attached, and the next POST 400s or the model is told it can see an image it cannot.

Host backends already refuse or ignore `--image` (`cursor` errors, `codex` status-and-ignore, `acp` client errors). The native loop has no equivalent capability bit, so TUI Ctrl-V / `/image` and `tny ask --image` also hit those providers.

This is the same shape as `--fast` ([ADR 0010](https://github.com/thehumanworks/tny/blob/main/docs/adr/0010-fast-tier-capability.md)): advertise a capability, map it per provider, fail closed when missing.

## Required outcome

- Add a capability bit, e.g. `TNY_CAP_IMAGES` in `tny_backend_caps` (`src/core/backend.h` / `src/core/backend.c`). OpenAI-compatible backends that accept vision parts set it; host backends (cursor, codex, acp) do not unless a later issue wires image input.
- Native-loop **named providers** need a per-profile override. Default: capability on (current behavior). A profile / env / model that cannot take images must be able to clear the bit (settings field and/or `NAME_IMAGES=0`). Builtin `grok` chat-proxy and other known text-only paths should default off unless proven otherwise; do not guess at runtime from a 400.
- When the bit is off:
  - `tools_schema_json` omits `read_image`.
  - `read_image` / `vision` execution returns a clear tool error (“this provider cannot view images”) instead of queuing pixels.
  - `read_file` on an image file still refuses binary dump, but the error must **not** tell the model to call `read_image`.
  - `tny ask --image`, TUI `/image`, and Ctrl-V image paste fail with a one-line reason **before** the turn starts (exit 1 on CLI), listing how to switch provider. Do not POST the data URL.
- When the bit is on, current ADR 0008 behavior is unchanged (schema, flush, `--image`).
- wasm: same gate; the browser native loop uses this bit. State the behavior on `docs/backends/openai-compatible.md` and `docs/tui.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tny_backend_caps` grows `TNY_CAP_IMAGES`. Unit test in `tests/test_core.c` asserts openai has it by default and cursor/codex/acp do not.
- [ ] A settings/env override can clear the bit for a named openai-compatible profile; `tools_schema_json` then contains no `read_image` function.
- [ ] `tools_execute(..., "read_image", …)` on a no-image env returns `error:` and leaves `n_pending_images == 0`. `read_file` on a png still errors, without mentioning `read_image`.
- [ ] `tny ask --image file.png` against a no-image provider exits 1 with a one-line reason and does not start a turn (integration or unit at the ask/engine boundary).
- [ ] TUI `/image` and Ctrl-V on a no-image provider print a system/note line and do not queue `t->images`.
- [ ] Existing `read_image_queues_user_message` stays green for the default openai path.
- [ ] Docs: `docs/cli.md`, `docs/tui.md`, `docs/backends/openai-compatible.md`, `docs/adr/0008-native-loop-images.md` (consequences / pointer to the new bit). New ADR only if the settings schema or default-off list is a durable policy; otherwise extend 0008.
- [ ] wasm behavior stated (works; same C gate). `make test` passes.

## Non-goals

- Teaching cursor/codex/acp to accept `--image` (host image input is a separate Cursor/Codex issue).
- Auto-detecting vision from a failed POST or from model-id heuristics.
- Changing MIME sniffing, 8 MiB cap, or the user-role `image_url` encoding.

## References

- `src/core/backend.h` — `TNY_CAP_FAST` pattern
- `src/core/tools.c` — `SCHEMA_JSON`, `tools_schema_json`, `tools_flush_images`
- `src/core/tools_ext.c` — `t_read_image`
- `src/core/tools_fs.c` / `src/core/tools_ssh.c` — `read_file` image refusal
- `src/core/image.c` — `session_add_user_images`
- `src/tui/tui_input.c` — `do_paste` / Ctrl-V
- `src/tui/tui_commands.c` — `/image`
- `src/cli/cmd_ask.c` — `--image`
- `src/backends/openai/openai.c` — `oa_send` image attach
- `tests/test_core.c` — `read_image_queues_user_message`, `tny_backend_caps` tests
- `docs/adr/0008-native-loop-images.md`, `docs/adr/0010-fast-tier-capability.md`
